original_observation: Fava and Sigrist 2008 population study reports Apis mellifera high visitation but failure to promote fruit set and Bombus sp. lower visitation yet effective stigma contact and pollen flow; fruit set lower under natural pollination than cross-hand pollination.
numeric_scope: Later independent study: Apis relative visitation 0.88; Bombus 0.13; natural fruit set 18% versus hand cross 76%; do not attribute to 1998 admission experiment.
main_uncertainty: 1998 Torezan-Silingardi/Del-Claro original full data not inspected; later independent study/field contexts need not be identical. Hand-cross fruit set not same as actual visitor-specific paternal fitness.
extra_evidence: 2008 author abstract, independently sampled original population

original_observation: Kirk 1987 quantified thrips feeding on Echium plantagineum and Actinidia deliciosa pollen; original 1984 separate Echium field observations describe larval hiding during sunshine and anther feeding in low light/at night. These are distinct experiments, not two independent replication taxa.
numeric_scope: Kirk 1987: mean 29-843 grains per thrips/day across treatments and source pollens; 1626-grain maximum for an individual Thrips imaginis larva on Echium; estimated 0.2-0.7% of average flower pollen per thrips/day across taxa.
main_uncertainty: Laboratory pollen loss does not establish stigma deposition or seed/siring fitness. Field 1984 light/visitor timing is a separately published source; do not overwrite original U6 SIMULTANEOUS pollen-pool tag.
extra_evidence: Admission shared DOI with Actinidia deliciosa; group-specific independent-study count cannot be two

original_observation: Vaughton 1996 finds nectar-seeking honeybees did not contact reproductive organs, while pollen collectors visited chiefly male-stage flowers; bird-exclusion cages permitting honeybees showed lower fruit set than bird+bee access, and were also worse than fully bagged flowers. This is direct source-controlled ecological visitor contrast, not randomized alternative architecture.
numeric_scope: Original published abstract: more than 50% lower fruit set in bee-access/bird-exclusion inflorescences relative to open inflorescences.
main_uncertainty: Male vs female floral developmental phases observed; source does not demonstrate cue-reversible within-flower state, structural module construction cost, new independent organ, or an evolutionary origin.
extra_evidence: Funded research publication reproduction of original Vaughton 1996 abstract

original_observation: Paciorek et al. 1995 original publication title specifically studies pollen consumption by hummingbird flower mites and possible fitness effects on Hamelia patens. Later separate Cutraro et al. 1998 primary laboratory flower-choice experiment shows Proctolaelaps kirmsei responds to stamens and nectaries, with no detected preference between pollen-only and nectar-only presentation.
numeric_scope: Original 1995 primary pollen-consumption numerical effect was NOT directly checked; a 2024 later literature summary reports approximately 5.4% and 16% pollen consumption estimates and cautions they may be overestimated. Neither value is a new source-recomputed effect.
main_uncertainty: The original Paciorek 1995 full study and quantitative pollen-fate assay were not accessible; do not promote secondhand 2024 values or 1998 laboratory attraction to stigma-transfer or male fitness, and retain U6 EVIDENCE_CEILING.
extra_evidence: Original paper identity verified at JSTOR and author website, separate 1998 original choice study and secondary 2024 summary

original_observation: Wilson and Thomson 1991 describe pollen-collecting Apis removing much pollen with little deposition, versus nectar-foraging Bombus removing less but depositing more. Young et al. 2007 revisited the species at a site where Apis was nectar-foraging, and the taxon difference disappeared when both bee types foraged similarly.
numeric_scope: No directly comparable controlled quantitative effect size extracted from the two different site/time studies; observational direction is source-confirmed by the 2007 authors.
main_uncertainty: Across-study visitor behaviour differs, with no manipulated genotype/architectural alternatives and no direct evolutionary transition; full Wilson/Thomson 1991 numeric tables not reopened. Species is known U1 taxon overlap.
extra_evidence: Independent 2007 single-visit pollen and seed study identifies behaviour as alternative to species identity

original_observation: Gross and Mackay 1998 report Apis mellifera workers collected deposited pollen from stigmatic surfaces rather than from source anthers; native bees deposited more pollen; seed/fruit set lower if honeybees visited last, and introduced bees disrupted native-bee visits.
numeric_scope: Original 1998 abstract: in 91% of honeybee-native-bee interactions native bees were displaced; source reports significantly lower seed set with Apis as last visitor, but raw effects/CI not recovered.
main_uncertainty: This is an explicitly post-deposition recipient-stigma loss, not verified same-anther source-pool consumption; frozen U6 source-pollen coordinate needs independent location adjudication. POWO places M. affine D.Don under M. malabathricum subspecies, creating U3 accepted-taxon dependence; study populations not proven same.
extra_evidence: Original publisher abstract/discussion accessible; University of New England institutional author abstract agrees
